docs/stylesheets.candidate: Translucent blurred header with hairline divider and shadow on scroll
Heading weights, letter-spacing and tab link opacity
Tables styled as cards with uppercase headers
Bold nav title and active nav link
Footer background and muted link colour

s3-backup-sidecar/backup.candidate: Repository password and cloud credentials are read by restic itself from the environment, with a missing password failing in restic
Heartbeat request uses a 10-second timeout and discards the body
Verification reads exactly a 5% subset per run
Plain-text 'backup: ...' progress lines for each step
Backup paths are word-split so paths with spaces cannot be named
Init attempted on any config-read failure (wrong password, unreachable store)

s3-backup-sidecar/dockerfile.candidate: Tool versions pinned via ARG with base image pinned by digest
pipefail makes a failed restic download fail the build instead of shipping an empty binary
Per-architecture binary download via TARGETARCH (defaults to amd64)
Two-stage build (fetch stage, then a slim runtime stage)
supercronic bundled as the cron scheduler
curl and ca-certificates installed in the runtime image (used for heartbeat pings and TLS)
s3-backup-sidecar/dockerfile.source: Dockerfile#RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates tini tzdata curl

s3-backup-sidecar/dockerfile.candidate: backup.sh and entrypoint.sh installed on the PATH; run-mode dispatch belongs to the entrypoint module
Bind-mounted /backups that is not writable is refused at startup with guidance
The image declares its Apache-2.0 licence and ships its notice

s3-backup-sidecar/entrypoint.candidate: Schedule is written to /tmp/crontab and handed to supercronic
Scheduler runs with -json so its output is structured JSON
Each mode replaces the shell via exec so signals reach the child
Preflight probes with `restic cat config` before trying `restic init`
Fresh named volume at /backups is writable by uid 10001
Explicit `cron` argument behaves like no argument

s3-backup-sidecar/makefile.candidate: `make` with no target lists every target with its one-line description
`make build` builds the image tagged <IMAGE>:<version from version.txt>
`make lint` runs every pre-commit hook on every file
`make test` builds the image, then runs test.sh against that tag
`make install` pulls the published image at the version in version.txt
`make run` builds the image and runs it with ARGS as the container arguments
`make format` runs the whitespace, end-of-file and line-ending fixers and ignores their non-zero exits
`make analyze` stops with exit 69 and an install link when trivy is missing, otherwise scans the tree for CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and secrets
`make push` builds the image and pushes the version tag

`make release` builds amd64+arm64 with buildx and pushes the version and latest tags. The images operators actually pull are published by .github/workflows/publish.yml, so that tag and architecture promise belongs to the CI module, not here

s3-backup-sidecar/dockerfile.rule: The sidecar never runs as root: every process runs as uid 10001
A fresh named volume at /backups can be written to, so the first backup does not fail with a permission error
